A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, algorithms and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, analytical regret bounds and mathematical proofs, including in its appendices. Its comparison tables contain theoretical guarantees, not original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Neither the main text nor the appendices report experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The OFTRL updates, optimistic estimators, log-barrier regularizers, loss shifting, dilated bonuses and virtual-episode mechanism are retained. The algorithms exchange numbers, and global-optimization pseudocode moves from Appendix D to Section 4; these are not procedural changes.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluated tasks. The revised stochastic MDP instances in Appendix G are mathematical lower-bound constructions, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Tables 1–3 compare theoretical guarantees for the same cited methods; the Dann et al. year-letter changes do not identify different methods.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols or evaluation settings are reported in either version. Changes to horizon requirements in Section 6 and Appendix G are theorem assumptions.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or case studies. The appendices provide notation, related-work discussion and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, empirical confidence intervals or significance tests. Revisions to Appendix F's concentration arguments concern theoretical proofs.

E6.justification: There are no measured scores, rankings or observed outcomes in either version. Changes to symbolic regret guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix G substantially revises the lower-bound argument: Lemma G.2 corrects the dependence on S and changes T ≥ A/(8H) to T ≥ SA/(8H), while Theorem G.6 replaces the variable-mean Bernoulli construction with scaled losses from a Bernoulli(1/2) base instance. Appendix E repairs the action-wise squared-error argument and bonus bounds. Theorems 5.2–5.3 sharpen the principal additive remainder from H^2 S^2 A log^2(T) to H^(5/2) S^(3/2) A log^2(T), with corresponding appendix revisions. These materially revise formal guarantees and their mathematical support.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same headline contributions: refined data- and variance-dependent guarantees for known-transition MDPs using global and policy optimization, supported by lower bounds. The new conclusion restates these contributions; the leading regret orders remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces its blanket minimax-optimality statement with one restricted to first-order, second-order and variance-aware gap-independent bounds, aligning it with the path-length gap already acknowledged in v1 Section 6. The estimator discussion also explicitly qualifies optimism as applying to real episodes.

D1.justification: Section 2.2 newly specifies xi = 1/4 throughout the paper, whereas v1 leaves the step size within an interval. This supplies a concrete hyperparameter choice for the existing predictor, without establishing a different implementation or experiment.

R1.justification: The cited literature is retained, but Appendix G.1 now presents the base lower bound as an existing result rather than a generalized result. Table 1 also revises the displayed Jin et al. (2021) bound, restricting the minimum gap to suboptimal actions and dropping the additional HSA log(T) term.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the known-transition motivation and estimator discussion, and numerous mathematical cross-references are corrected. v2 adds a Conclusion and Impact Statement, introduces numbered subsections within Section 3, and relocates the global algorithm; most exposition and proof organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout with running headers and revised typography. Tables and algorithm blocks are resized or repositioned, including moving global-optimization pseudocode from the appendix into the main text. The four tables and two algorithms are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs consequential gaps in the paper's central theoretical support. Appendix G corrects the state-count dependence and replaces the problematic small-variance construction with loss rescaling; Appendix E replaces an invalid action-wise inequality with a valid summed-action bound. These changes substantially improve confidence in the lower-bound and policy-optimization claims, alongside sharper remainder terms. The stronger horizon requirement narrows the stated lower-bound coverage but makes it better supported. The main benefit is mathematical reliability, beyond the extensive reformatting.
